title: Catch mistakes with Checks
description: Make the mistakes that break real Ansible runs on purpose, then let Checks find them and fix them one by one.
outcomes: Read the Checks badge, its errors, warnings and notes
Jump from an issue straight to the component that causes it
Understand why host vars override group vars
Handle two components writing the same file, and undo a removal
recap: Each form catches its own mistakes, like a duplicate host name, before you save.
Checks catches the ones between components: groups nobody defines, hosts with two addresses, overrides.
Errors break the output, warnings are probably mistakes, notes are good to know.
Open on an issue jumps to the culprit, and the editor lists its issues at the top.
A file has one writer: kikx asks before replacing, and Undo brings back a removed component.

steps.intro: Ansible rarely complains when your files disagree with each other: a play aimed at the wrong group just does nothing. Let's make that kind of mistake on purpose and watch kikx catch it.
steps.name: A fresh project to break safely.
steps.inventory: Start with an inventory, the list of servers.
steps.hostGroup: One web server, in a group. Plays will target the group, not the server.
steps.addHost: Now a second server. Watch what happens if I copy the first one's name by accident.
steps.duplicate: Same name as the first host...
steps.formCatch: The form flags it right away. A host name must be unique, otherwise Ansible merges both rows into one machine.
steps.rename: Mistakes inside a single form never reach your project. Let me give it its own name.
steps.connection: Each host can carry its own connection settings.
steps.hostUser: Say someone set a login user on this host, months ago, for a quick test.
steps.groupRow: Now give the whole group its shared settings.
steps.groupVar: The team agreed every web server logs in as this user.
steps.quiet: The files render fine. Nothing here looks wrong, yet the two users disagree. Keep that in mind.
steps.playbook: Next, a playbook: it says which roles run on which group.
steps.wrongHosts: A classic slip: the play targets a short name instead of the real group.
steps.savePlaybook: Add it. Every file is valid on its own, so nothing stops us.
steps.badge: But the Checks tab now shows a number: issues found across your components, counting errors and warnings.
steps.playRow: Here is the play: it targets a group no inventory defines, so it would match zero hosts and silently do nothing.
steps.note: Notes are just good to know. This one says the role is not in the project yet, and offers a fix.
steps.scaffold: One click creates an empty role folder for it, and the note is gone.
steps.openRow: Every issue links to the components involved. Open takes you straight to the culprit.
steps.inline: The editor repeats the issue at the top, so you can fix it where it happens.
steps.fixHosts: Your turn: aim the play at the real group, then save. Watch the Checks count drop.
steps.oneLeft: One warning is left. Back to the Checks.
steps.override: Remember those two users? A host var always wins over a group var, so this host ignores the team's user without any error.
steps.openInventory: Open the inventory to fix it.
steps.inherit: Empty means inherit. Clearing this field lets the host take the group's user again.
steps.clearUser: Your turn: clear the host's SSH user, save, then open the Checks tab.
steps.clear: All clear. Hosts, groups and plays line up again.
steps.secondInventory: Some mistakes only show up between components. Let's add a second inventory, say for staging.
steps.otherAddress: Same server name as before, but a different address.
steps.redBadge: The badge turns red: that is an error, not a warning.
steps.twoAddresses: One host name now points at two machines. Ansible keeps whichever it reads last, so a deploy could hit the wrong server.
steps.toBuild: The fix here is to remove the extra inventory.
steps.remove: Removing is one click on the trash icon of its row.
steps.undone: And one click on Undo in the notification brings it back, files and all. The error is back too.
steps.removeAgain: We really want it gone, so remove it once more.
steps.groupVars: Last one: shared settings for the group, as their own file.
steps.saveGroupVars: Add them. This component writes one file named after the group.
steps.again: Now a teammate adds settings for the same group, not knowing they exist.
steps.liveWarning: Before even saving, kikx warns that this would replace a file another component already writes.
steps.saveAnyway: Let's try to add it anyway.
steps.dialog: A project has exactly one writer per file, so kikx asks first instead of silently keeping the last one.
steps.diff: Current on the left, incoming on the right. Only the value differs.
steps.keep: Keep existing leaves the first component alone. Replace would remove it and use the new one.
steps.done: That is the habit: build, glance at the badge, open the issue, fix it at the source. Checks never change your files on their own.

checks.hosts: The play runs on the real group
checks.count: Saved, and Checks shows one warning
